#1906. Red card for football chiefs as they announce ex-Premier League referee is dead aged 78 - when he is still alive and kicking

Published: 13:01 EST, 14 November 2026 | Updated: 20:45 EST, 14 November 2026

A former Premier League referee was mistakenly declared dead by football chiefs this week.

On Tuesday, the Football Association of Wales (FAW) announced Keith Cooper had died aged 78. But he is alive and well.

The news reached the ears of the Wembley Cup final referee when he went out to his local sports centre for a flu jab only to be told: 'You were dead.'

The Football Association of Wales posted a statement online and a tribute on social media to announce his death, but then withdrew it within an hour.

Mr Cooper, who is the father of former Nottingham Forest and Leicester boss Steve Cooper, told a Welsh sports website: 'I walked into the sports centre yesterday to have my jab and the fellow went, "You were dead!"

'Well, I'm not dead, I'm here and I'm OK!'

The blunder appears to have emerged after the Wiltshire FA announced the death of another referee called Keith Cooper, who the football chiefs in Wales believed was the other Keith Cooper.

The FAW statement said: 'Keith was a well-known figure who enjoyed an exceptional career at both domestic and international level and would later hold the position of FAW Referees' Officer following his retirement in 1996.

On Tuesday, the Football Association of Wales (FAW) announced Keith Cooper had died aged 78

Mark Beeney goalkeeper of Leeds United is Sent Off of by Referee Keith A Cooper for hand ball outside the area during the Premier League match between Manchester United and Leeds United at Old Trafford on April 17, 1996 in Manchester, England

Former professional football John Fashanu is pictured with referee Keith Cooper during a Wimbledon F.C. match

'Born and raised in Pontypridd, he is considered one of Wales' best match officials through his highly-regarded status in the game.

'In addition to his work with FAW, Keith was also a valued member of the Wiltshire FA Council who recognised his 'integrity, passion and commitment' in their tribute to his services to the game.

'Everyone at the FAW sends their condolences to his family and friends at this sad time.'

Mr Cooper oversaw the 1994 League Cup final between Aston Villa and Manchester United, won by Villa 3-1, and worked in radio punditry after hanging up his whistle.

The FAW has not issued an explanation over the posted tribute. His family has not yet commented on the error.

But the unfortunate mistake has not spared the FAW from ridicule by other football fans.

One said: 'We always said there was only one Keith Cooper - turns out there are two.'

Another said: 'Glad the whistle wasn't blown too early on Keith and much respect to the family of the other one.'

#1903. Union Berlin vs RB Leipzig - prediction, team news, lineups

By Sebastian Sternik | 20 Nov 2026 07:20

Union Berlin are in the midst of their second-worst start to a Bundesliga season, and things are not about to get any easier as the relegation contenders prepare to host an in-form RB Leipzig side this Saturday afternoon.

While Die Eisernen are languishing in the bottom three, Die Roten Bullen are eyeing up a fourth straight league victory as they continue to chase the Bundesliga’s top two.

With just seven points to their name from their opening nine Bundesliga matches, Union Berlin are already feeling the pressure.

Head coach Mauro Lustrinelli survived the international break, with the club's hierarchy seemingly prepared to give the Swiss tactician more time to turn things around.

However, his long-term future remains far from certain, particularly after director Horst Heldt cast doubt over whether the 47-year-old would still be in charge over the next five months.

Heldt also revealed that Union are already drawing up plans for the January transfer window, although with more than a month to go before it opens, any potential reinforcements are unlikely to provide Lustrinelli with immediate relief.

What may help the Swiss coach is the fact Union’s best results this season have come at home, with 86% of all their points coming at the Stadion An der Alten Forsterei.

Nevertheless, Union's defensive problems overshadow any slight positives, given they have already conceded 21 goals - a new club record at this stage of a Bundesliga campaign.

While Union struggle to keep the ball out of the net, RB Leipzig simply cannot stop scoring at the moment.

Martin Demichelis and his men have already rattled the net 27 times in the Bundesliga this season - a total only bettered by Bayern Munich, who have scored on 29 occasions.

Just before the international break, Leipzig put five goals past Augsburg in a 5-2 victory - a game which extended their winning run to three straight league matches.

In recent times, Leipzig have also seen an upswing in their away results, winning their last two competitive games on the road - including a 2-0 success against Schalke at the end of October.

Striking early has been the key for Die Rotten Bullen so far this season, with the club yet to drop a point when scoring first in the Bundesliga.

In fact, the only major concern ahead of Saturday’s game is the fact Leipzig have lost four of their last six trips to Stadion An der Alten Forsterei.

French defender Stanley Nsoki has missed every game this season for Union Berlin due to a muscle injury, and the 27-year-old will remain on the sidelines this weekend.

Robert Skov has only played one competitive minute this term, though he has recently returned to individual training.

Youngster Andrik Markgraf also remains out of action due to a knee injury, while Janik Haberer could miss Saturday’s game through illness.

When it comes to RB Leipzig, the visitors are also dealing with a handful of injuries as we head towards the end of the calendar year.

German midfielder Assan Ouedraogo has been out of action since September with a shoulder problem.

Youngsters Viggo Gebel and Marc Guiu are also dealing with knee and hamstring injuries.

Max Finkgrafe, meanwhile, has missed his last five games with a thigh injury, but is on the brink of a return.

Antonio Nusa, who has 11 goal contributions in nine Bundesliga games this season, is the man to watch for the visitors.

‘But the earliest Mauricio Pochettino can unravel this squad is two seasons if he does well. It could take three to get this squad unravelled.’

#1899. TNT Sports Brazil: Milan prepare €70m Endrick offer to Real Madrid – loan ‘off the table’

A report in Brazil has claimed that AC Milan have made an offer to Real Madrid for Endrick, and it is for a permanent deal.

In the past few weeks, there has been a lot of speculation suggesting that Milan are lining up a winter move for Endrick. He seems to be a player that the owner Gerry Cardinale personally likes, and the funds are available to at least make an attempt.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

According to Vitor Sergio of TNT Sports Brazil, Milan have begun talks with Madrid and Endrick’s representatives and are expected to submit a total offer of €70m for him. This would be €60m in fixed money, and €10m in add-ons. He adds that a loan is ‘off the table’.

In addition, the Rossoneri know they need to substantially increase the Brazilian’s salary. He currently receives around €3.2m net per season. Milan are aware of the figures involved in this deal and believe they have the financial capacity to pursue it.

To seal the deal, Real Madrid would also reportedly ask for two clauses with the future in mind. The first would given them the option to buy Endrick back for €85m (with only the length of the buy-back window still to be decided).

The second would allow Real to match a future offer, with the aim of reducing the chances of Endrick joining Barcelona or another elite European club in the future.

Although Los Blancos are willing to negotiate with the Diavolo, the Spanish club remains uncertain about selling the 20-year-old, as Mourinho still wants to count on him.

#1898. Xabi Alonso's January transfer plan dealt cruel blow as Chelsea 'barred' from signing £30m maestro

By Lewis Blain | 20 Nov 2026 07:31, Last updated: 20 Nov 2026 07:32

Chelsea have seen their hopes of signing Juventus youngster Kerim Alajbegovic hit a major stumbling block ahead of the January transfer window.

The Blues were previously interested in the teenager during the summer, with Blues boss Xabi Alonso having monitored his development closely during his time in charge of Bayer Leverkusen.

However, Juventus are determined to keep hold of the highly-rated winger, with a potential departure currently considered off the table.

Alajbegovic was pursued by Chelsea during the summer after impressing at RB Salzburg, but the west London club's proposed project failed to convince the youngster.

The Blues were understood to be considering sending him out on loan rather than offering immediate first-team opportunities, allowing the Serie A giants to secure his signature instead.

There has now been renewed interest from Alonso's side, but reports in Italy (via Sport Witness) suggest Chelsea face an uphill battle to bring the 19-year-old maestro to Stamford Bridge.

It is claimed that Alajbegovic 'isn't leaving' Juventus, with the Italian side pleased by his development and unwilling to consider an exit despite interest from England.

The £30m teenager is also happy with his role in Turin, where he believes he has the right environment to continue developing, with similar reports suggesting that he wants to remain at Juventus for a 'long time'.

As a result, an immediate departure has been described as 'truly barred', making a January transfer particularly difficult to negotiate.

Chelsea's interest is understandable given the Bosnian's potential, but the club may struggle to convince him that Stamford Bridge is the right place for his development.

Regular first-team football should be a priority for a teenager at this stage of his career, and Juventus are currently providing him with opportunities to establish himself.

By contrast, Chelsea's sizeable squad creates greater competition for attacking positions, with even highly-rated youngster Estevao having experienced his own difficulties securing consistent game time.

That situation could serve as a warning to Alajbegovic, particularly when he is already enjoying an increasingly prominent role in Turin.

Although Juventus may not offer the most stable environment, they are giving the youngster opportunities to develop at senior level.

Chelsea might be able to offer a lucrative project, but unless they can guarantee a clearer pathway into the first team, Alajbegovic would arguably be better off remaining in Italy.

Moises Caicedo has revealed he asked to be substituted at half-time playing for Ecuador as Chelsea were handed a scare during the international break.

Ecuador played friendly matches against Costa Rica and Bolivia, picking up 2-0 victories in both games.

Caicedo played 84 minutes in Quito in what was Marcelo Gallardo’s first game in charge on Saturday, named in the starting XI again on Tuesday.

The former Brighton star was replaced halfway through that game, later revealing he was ‘not feeling well’ with Chelsea’s game against Leeds United on Saturday in his thoughts.

‘No, I didn’t feel very well, so I asked to come off instead, because I know I have another commitment with my club.,’ Caicedo told reporters. ‘So, I’ll try to get there as soon as possible and recover.’

He was ruled out of the next three games but has started Chelsea’s last five in the Premier League.

During the international break, the 25-year-old opened up on his recent fitness issues.

#1896. ‘Wasted’ – Paul Ince questions £50m Man Utd transfer decision

Paul Ince still cannot wrap his head around Manchester United’s decision to spend £50million on Andrey Santos in the summer transfer window.

Santos completed a £50m move from Chelsea over the summer, arriving alongside Youri Tielemans and Carlos Baleba as the Red Devils sought to bolster their depth in central midfield.

Santos enjoyed an encouraging pre-season, but started only four of United’s first ten Premier League matches under Michael Carrick before his sacking.

Mauricio Pochettino’s arrival may represent a fresh start for the £50m midfielder, but Ince believes United would have been better served spending that money elsewhere over the summer.

‘Why did they spend £50m on Santos?’ Ince told The Sun. ‘That’s £50m wasted. They could have put that into the defence or bought a striker.

Read exclusive analysis of the biggest stories in football with Metro's weekly football newsletter In The Mixer. Sign up now for free.

‘They have [Kobbie] Mainoo, who needs to develop. He needs to be playing, not Santos.

‘Tielemans, again, fantastic at Villa but it’s a different conversation when you come to United.

‘Baleba didn’t play a lot last year. He comes in for £70m, plays a couple of games and he’s injured again.

‘The game’s changing. It’s not all pass, pass, pass now. You’ve got to win your duels. You used to hear Pep Guardiola say every time, “We didn’t win our duels, we didn’t win our tackles”.

‘The game’s more physical, more powerful.’

#1895. Family's fury as 'elite' athlete twin brothers are arrested by ICE while on their way to college in Alabama

Published: 20:42 EST, 14 November 2026 | Updated: 21:42 EST, 14 November 2026

A dismayed mother and father spoke out after their 'elite' athlete twin sons were arrested by Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) as they returned to their Alabama college.

Wallace State Community College soccer players Luis and Carlos Orta Santoro, 19, were taken into ICE custody after a traffic stop on November 4 while on their way to campus, the Atlanta Journal-Constitution reported.

The Venezuelan twins were returning from visiting their parents, Carlos Enrique Orta and Reyna Santoro de Orta, in Georgia when they were arrested by a Lincoln Police Department officer during a traffic stop in east-central Alabama.

The brothers graduated from Lawrenceville's Archer High School after a successful varsity soccer career that included a first ever region title for the school.

'This is the house of two elite soccer players,' Carlos Enrique Orta, their father, told the outlet.

Luis and Carlos are asylum seekers who applied for protections after legally entering the US on a tourist visa, like their parents.

That visa expired and the twins were granted US work permits and Georgia driver's licenses, according to the outlet.

A spokesperson for the Department of Homeland Security (DHS), which oversees ICE, told the Daily Mail on Saturday that the brothers had legally entered the US with permission to stay on a temporary basis on June 21, 2022, but then 'illegally overstayed in defiance of our laws.'

Twin brothers and soccer players Luis and Carlos Orta Santoro, both 19, were taken into ICE custody on November 5 after being arrested the previous day

Luis and Carlos were region title-winning soccer players for Archer High School in Lawrenceville, Georgia

The brothers were arrested as they returned from visiting their parents, Carlos Enrique Orta and Reyna Santoro de Orta (both left)

The DHS spokesperson told the Daily Mail: 'All their claims will be heard by an immigration judge, and they will receive due process. This administration will not ignore the rule of law.'

'To be clear, pending applications do NOT confer legal status,' the statement continued.

Carlos was named the offensive player of the year and Luis the midfield player of the year by their high school this year.

They had received soccer scholarships to attend Wallace State, which they began doing this fall, but now face deportation to Venezuela.

'It's been hell,' Santoro de Orta, their mother, told the outlet.

She added that she supported ICE 'taking away the criminals' but said her children did not fit that description.

A final decision on the brothers' asylum case is still pending as they remain in custody.

The concerned mother claimed police said the twins' car had failed to come to a complete stop at a stop sign.

The brothers were arrested by a Lincoln Police Department officer as they were returning to Wallace State Community College, where they have soccer scholarships

The family applied for asylum protections after legally entering the country on a tourist visa. The DHS said the brothers 'illegally overstayed in defiance of our laws'

The Lincoln Police Department signed a partnership agreement with ICE in July.

ICE said the program allows trained local officers to exercise limited immigration authority during routine police work under federal supervision, according to the Cullman Tribune.

Luis and Carlos were booked into the Talladega County Jail on November 4 and transferred to ICE custody the following day.

Their father, Orta, described how the family was grappling with guilt as they shared what happened to their children.

'If anyone is at fault, it's me. It's us,' Orta told the outlet. 'Because I insist and I will continue to insist that Carlos and Luis came here because of a decision we made.'

He added: 'Carlos and Luis stayed here because of a decision from mom and dad. Carlos and Luis are here because of us.'

The Santoro twins were taken to the Pine Prairie ICE Processing Center in southern Louisiana after their arrest, WABE reported.

The brothers have been taken to the the Pine Prairie ICE Processing Center in southern Louisiana

The Lincoln Police Department signed an partnership agreement with ICE in July. A department officer arrested the brothers

A friend of the twins, Nicolas Azcarate Florez, said he had spoken to them multiple times since they were taken into custody.

'They've been saying that they've been moved five times, so it has been difficult for them,' Azcarate Florez told the outlet.

Azcarate Florez said the brothers were 'players that you could just give the ball to, and you would know that they would do something good with it.'

'If we needed them, we would know that they would be there to help us out of a sticky situation,' he added.

The brothers were taken into custody on the same week that the Republican Party faced a historic blue wave in the midterm elections that was seen as a rebuke of the GOP's immigration policy.

One of President Donald Trump's first moves afterwards was to name Stephen Miller as the new White House chief of staff, replacing Susie Wiles.

Miller, one of Trump's most loyal and longest-serving advisers going back to his first administration, is known for his hardline views on immigration.

Critics have cited Miller as the architect of some of Trump's most divisive policies, including separating migrant families during deportations in the President's first term.
